script.content: The emergency broadcast on your phone didn't end with instructions; it ended with a wet, choking scream that cut to static just as the power grid blew, plunging your apartment into an oppressive, heavy darkness. Outside your third-story window, the familiar hum of the city has mutated into a chaotic symphony of screeching tires, distant explosions, and an underlying, rhythmic scuffling sound that makes the hairs on your arms stand up.
A frantic, heavy pounding suddenly rattles your front door, accompanied by the panicked voice of your neighbor, Mrs. Gutierrez, begging to be let in.
Please! Oh God, please let me in! They're in the building! They got Mr. Chen from 2B! I saw... I saw them *tear* him apart!
From the alleyway directly below your fire escape, you hear the unmistakable sound of breaking glass and a guttural, distinctly non-human howl. You have moments to decide.

choices.label: Open the door for Mrs. Gutierrez
choices.description: You rush to the front door, fumbling with the locks. Mrs. Gutierrez is terrified and alone in the hallway. You can't leave her out there to die. But opening the door means letting in whatever else might be lurking in the hallway too.
choices.targetSceneDescription: The door swings open and Mrs. Gutierrez stumbles inside, sobbing with relief. But as you slam the door shut, you hear heavy, scrabbling footsteps in the hallway. Something is coming. You're now trapped inside your apartment with a panicking elderly woman, and the infected are right outside your door.

choices.label: Take the fire escape to the rooftop
choices.description: Your instincts scream at you: stay quiet, stay hidden. You quickly drag your bookshelf in front of the front door, muffling her desperate cries with guilt, and scramble toward the fire escape window. Below, shapes move in the alley. You'll have to go up, to the rooftop.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You climb out onto the rusted fire escape, your hands shaking. The metal groans beneath you. As you climb upward toward the rooftop, you hear the front door of your apartment splinter open below. Mrs. Gutierrez's scream is cut short. You force yourself to keep climbing.

choices.label: Tell her to hide, grab supplies, and prepare
choices.description: You press your mouth against the door and whisper urgently through it, telling Mrs. Gutierrez to hide in the stairwell closet while you grab supplies. You can't just open the door blind. You need a weapon, a plan. You start frantically grabbing anything useful—a kitchen knife, a flashlight, your backpack.
choices.targetSceneDescription: Armed with makeshift supplies and a rough plan, you crack open the door. The hallway is empty and eerily silent—until you hear a wet, choking sound from the stairwell. Mrs. Gutierrez didn't make it to the closet. Something got her. The infected are already moving through the building.

script.content: You throw open the door and Mrs. Gutierrez stumbles inside, sobbing. Her floral nightgown is torn, and there's a dark smear of blood on her cheek—not hers, you realize with a jolt. She's shaking uncontrollably as you slam the door shut and throw the deadbolt.
They're everywhere! In the halls! I saw them take Mr. Chen—they just *swarmed* him! Oh God, oh God, we're going to die!

Heavy, wet thuds begin slamming against your front door. The wood groans. Through the peephole, you see a nightmare—a face pressed against the door, eyes white and rolling, mouth gaping, fingers scrabbling at the wood until the nails tear away. More shapes lurch into view behind it.
The door won't hold forever. You have two choices: barricade yourselves here and fight, or take Mrs. Gutierrez with you out the fire escape window.

choices.label: Barricade the apartment and make a stand
choices.description: You shout at Mrs. Gutierrez to help you drag the sofa, the bookshelf, everything against the door. If you can hold them off, maybe help will come. Maybe you can survive here.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You and Mrs. Gutierrez pile furniture against the door, creating a makeshift barricade. The infected pound relentlessly. You grab a kitchen knife and wait, heart pounding in your ears. Then you hear scratching at the fire escape window behind you.

choices.label: Escape through the fire escape with Mrs. Gutierrez
choices.description: You grab Mrs. Gutierrez by the hand and drag her toward the fire escape window. 'We're going up!' you hiss. The fire escape leads to the rooftop—maybe from there you can find a way down or signal for help.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You help Mrs. Gutierrez onto the fire escape. The metal groans ominously as you both climb. Below, shapes lurch through the alley. Above, the rooftop offers uncertain safety. Halfway up, the fire escape shudders violently—something below is climbing after you.

script.content: You scramble up the rusted fire escape, your breath ragged in your throat. Behind you, from your apartment, Mrs. Gutierrez's scream pierces the night—then cuts off with a sickening abruptness. Guilt crashes over you like a wave, but survival instinct keeps you climbing.

You haul yourself onto the rooftop. The wind hits you hard, carrying the smell of smoke and the distant sounds of chaos. The city burns on the horizon, a hellish panorama of orange and black. For a moment, you're alone under the open sky.
But you're not alone. A shape moves near the rooftop's edge—a man. He turns at the sound of your arrival, brandishing a crowbar. It's Marcus, the guy from the second floor with the motorcycle.
You from the building? Anyone else make it?

choices.label: Tell Marcus the truth about Mrs. Gutierrez
choices.description: You confess what you did—that you left your neighbor to die while you escaped. Marcus's face is unreadable in the dim light. You need to know if you can trust him.
choices.targetSceneDescription: Marcus listens to your confession in silence. Then he nods grimly. 'Hard choices are all that's left now,' he says. He tells you the building is surrounded. He's been planning an escape route through the adjacent building's rooftop. But the gap between buildings is treacherous.

choices.label: Ask Marcus if he has a plan
choices.description: You don't have time for guilt. You ask Marcus directly what he knows and if he has a way out. He seems capable, and you need allies.
choices.targetSceneDescription: Marcus jerks his thumb toward the adjoining building. 'Fire escape on that side is clear. I've been watching. But we gotta cross the gap.' He shows you a wooden plank he found. 'It's our only shot. Or we stay here and wait for whatever comes next.'

choices.label: Stay silent and search for another way
choices.description: You don't answer Marcus. Trust is earned, and right now you don't trust anyone. You move past him to survey the rooftop for your own escape route.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You ignore Marcus and scout the rooftop perimeter. You spot a drainage pipe leading down to an alley, but it's slick with moisture. Below, you can hear the infected shuffling. Going solo means you answer to no one—but you also have no backup.

script.content: You grab your backpack and shove in whatever you can find in the dark—a flashlight, a first-aid kit, a box of granola bars, a bottle of water. From the kitchen drawer, you pull the largest knife you own. Your hands are shaking as you strap on your sneakers.
You press your ear to the front door. Silence. Mrs. Gutierrez isn't calling anymore. A cold knot forms in your stomach. You crack the door open, peering into the dark hallway.

The hallway is empty. Flickering emergency lights cast dancing shadows. The door to the stairwell is slightly ajar, and from within comes a wet, rhythmic sound—like something feeding. A sob catches in your throat. Mrs. Gutierrez didn't make it to the closet.

She's gone. They're in the stairwell. I can't go that way. The other end of the hallway leads to a window overlooking the street. Or I could try to fight through the stairwell and reach the ground floor. Either way, I have to move now.

choices.label: Head to the hallway window and climb down
choices.description: You creep to the window at the end of the hall. It overlooks a narrow side street. Below, overturned cars burn. A dumpster sits directly beneath the window. If you can drop onto it, you might make it to street level and find another path.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You force the window open and look down. The drop to the dumpster is risky but doable. Below, the street is a war zone—but you spot a pharmacy across the road with its doors smashed open. Supplies. Safety is nowhere, but survival might be found in the shadows.

choices.label: Fight through the stairwell
choices.description: The stairwell is the fastest route down, and there might be other survivors. You grip your knife, steel your nerves, and push through the stairwell door, ready to face whatever is feeding in the darkness.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You burst through the stairwell door, knife raised. The landing is a butcher's shop—blood and torn clothing everywhere. Two infected creatures crouch over a shape you refuse to look at. They turn toward you with a unified, horrible motion. You have nowhere to run but down.

script.content: You shout at Mrs. Gutierrez to help you. Together, you drag the sofa, the bookshelf, and the dining table against the door. The wood splinters as the infected throw themselves against it from the other side.
It's holding! It's holding! Oh please, Jesus, let it hold!

You back away from the door, your heart hammering. The pounding continues, rhythmic, relentless. But the barricade holds. You allow yourself a moment to breathe. Then you hear it—a metallic scrape from the fire escape window. Something is climbing up.

You whirl around. Through the grimy glass of the fire escape window, a pale hand slaps against the pane, leaving a bloody smear. A face presses against the glass—sunken eyes, gaping mouth. The infected are coming from both sides.
We're trapped! We're trapped!

choices.label: Fight the infected at the window
choices.description: You grab the kitchen knife and approach the window. If you can break the glass and stab the infected before it gets inside, you might be able to close it off. It's a risky gambit.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You shatter the window with a lamp and lunge at the infected creature clinging to the fire escape. The fight is brutal and desperate. You manage to push it off, but not before it claws your arm. Blood wells from the wound. Mrs. Gutierrez screams behind you. In the other room, the front door splinters.

choices.label: Try to escape out the window past the infected
choices.description: There's no winning this fight. You grab Mrs. Gutierrez and make a break for the window. There's one infected on the fire escape—maybe you can shove past it and climb to the rooftop before more come.

choices.label: Find a hiding spot in the apartment
choices.description: You pull Mrs. Gutierrez into the bedroom closet, pulling the doors shut, pressing your hands over her mouth. If you stay silent, maybe they'll pass through without finding you.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You and Mrs. Gutierrez huddle in the dark closet, barely breathing. The infected break through both entrances. You hear them shuffling through your apartment, knocking things over. One pauses right outside the closet door. You can hear it breathing—wet, labored rasps. Then it moves on.

script.content: You help Mrs. Gutierrez climb onto the fire escape. The old metal groans under your combined weight. Her hands are trembling so badly she nearly slips, but you catch her arm and guide her up the ladder.
Below, shapes lurch through the alley—three, maybe four infected, drawn by the noise. They haven't seen you yet, but it's only a matter of time. Above, the rooftop offers uncertain safety.

Halfway up, the fire escape shudders violently. A section of the ladder below breaks loose, clattering against the wall. The infected below look up and screech. They've seen you. They begin climbing after you, their movements jerky but fast.
Keep climbing! Don't stop!

choices.label: Pull Mrs. Gutierrez up to the rooftop
choices.description: You redouble your efforts, practically dragging Mrs. Gutierrez up the last few rungs. The infected are climbing fast, but you might make it if you work together.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You haul Mrs. Gutierrez onto the rooftop just as the first infected reaches the top of the ladder. You kick the ladder away, sending it crashing down into the alley. You're safe for now—but you're on the rooftop with a terrified elderly woman, and the ladder is gone. A man with a crowbar watches you from across the roof.

choices.label: Save yourself and leave Mrs. Gutierrez
choices.description: The infected are gaining. Mrs. Gutierrez is slowing you down. In a moment of terrible clarity, you realize you can't save both of you. You scramble ahead, leaving her behind.

script.content: You force the window open, gasping at the rush of cool, smoke-tinged air. Below, a dumpster sits against the wall—your landing pad. The drop is two stories. It'll hurt, but it won't kill you.

You swing your legs over the sill and drop. You hit the dumpster lid with a deafening CLANG, the impact jarring your knees and spine. Pain shoots up your leg as you roll off and tumble to the pavement.

You're on the street. Overturned cars burn nearby, casting flickering orange light. Across the road, you spot a pharmacy with its front window smashed in. Medical supplies, maybe food. A survivor's dream. But from the darkness of the store, you hear a low, wet growl.

choices.label: Enter the pharmacy for supplies
choices.description: Medical supplies are too valuable to pass up. You grip your weapon and step through the shattered glass into the dark pharmacy. The growl grows louder. Something is in there with you.
choices.targetSceneDescription: The pharmacy is dark and smells of medicine and decay. Shelves have been toppled. As your eyes adjust, you see a figure hunched over by the counter—an infected, feeding. It hasn't noticed you yet. The back room may have more supplies, but you'll have to get past it.

choices.label: Cross the street and keep moving toward a safer area
choices.description: Supplies mean nothing if you're dead. You decide to push forward, staying to the shadows, heading east where the fires seem less intense.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You move quickly through the burning streets, sticking to shadows and alleyways. You pass bodies and wreckage. After several blocks, you hear gunshots—not infected, but *human*. Someone else is alive out here, and they're fighting back.

script.content: You push through the stairwell door, knife raised, stomach churning.

The stairwell is a slaughterhouse. Blood paints the walls in grotesque arcs. Two infected crouch over a shape on the landing—a body you force yourself not to look at. Their heads snap toward you simultaneously, moving with an unnatural, fluid synchronization that makes your blood run cold.
They rise. They screech—a sound that tears through the stairwell like broken glass. And they charge.

choices.label: Fight them head-on
choices.description: You have a knife, and they're between you and the ground floor. There's no other way. You scream and lunge at the closest infected, driving the blade forward.
choices.targetSceneDescription: The fight is savage. You manage to stab one infected through the eye, but the other tackles you down the stairs. Pain explodes through your body. You and the infected tumble to the ground floor landing in a heap. You're wounded, but you made it to the bottom. The exit door is right there.

choices.label: Retreat back into the hallway
choices.description: There are two of them and one of you with a kitchen knife. Bravery is just another word for suicide. You slam the stairwell door shut and back away, looking for another route.

script.content: I left her. I heard her die. And I kept climbing. What kind of person does that make me?
I... I left my neighbor. Mrs. Gutierrez. She was at my door. I barricaded it and ran. She didn't make it.
Marcus listens in silence. The wind whips between you. Finally, he speaks.

Hard choices are all that's left now. You think I didn't leave people behind? My own damn brother—he got bit right in front of me. I had to put him down before he turned. This is the world now. You survive, or you don't. Don't let guilt get you killed.
He spits over the edge. 'The building is surrounded. But I've been watching next door. The gap between rooftops is about eight feet. I found a plank we can use to cross. You in?'

choices.label: Cross the gap with Marcus
choices.description: You accept Marcus's offer. Together, you drag the plank across the gap to the adjacent building. It's a terrifying crossing—one wrong step and you'll fall three stories into the alley below. But on the other side, there might be a way down.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You and Marcus cross to the adjacent building. Below, the infected mill about, unaware. You find a fire door leading inside. It's dark, but Marcus has a lighter. The building is a former office space—cubicles, shattered glass, and the smell of stale coffee. Something rustles in the darkness ahead.

choices.label: Refuse and go your own way
choices.description: You appreciate the offer, but you can't shake the feeling that you need to move alone. You tell Marcus you'll take your chances elsewhere. He shrugs, 'Suit yourself. Stay alive.' You head for the drainage pipe you spotted earlier.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You shimmy down the drainage pipe, your hands burning on the cold metal. You drop into a narrow alley behind a dumpster. Two infected are shuffling past, their backs to you. You freeze, holding your breath. They pass. You're on street level, alone, with the burning city stretching out before you.

script.content: What's the situation? You got a way out of this?

Marcus jerks his thumb toward the adjoining building—a slightly taller structure about eight feet away. 'Fire escape on that side is clear. I've been watching it for twenty minutes. Nothing's come out or gone up. But we gotta cross the gap first.'
He kicks a wooden plank at his feet—a long, sturdy piece of lumber, probably salvaged from a construction pile on the roof.

I found this. Lay it across, walk slow, don't look down. On the other side, we take the fire escape down to street level. From there... well, we play it by ear. There's a police station six blocks east. If any safe zone exists, it'll be there.
He looks at you hard. 'Or we stay here and wait for the cavalry. Your call. But I'm not waiting.'

choices.label: Cross to the next building with Marcus
choices.description: You help Marcus lay the plank across the gap. It wobbles precariously. One by one, you cross—heart pounding, eyes fixed forward. You make it. The fire escape on this side leads down to a dark alley.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You successfully cross to the adjacent building with Marcus. The fire door leads into a dark office building. Cubicles stretch into the darkness. As your eyes adjust, you see overturned chairs, papers scattered everywhere, and a vending machine with its glass front smashed. From somewhere in the dark, a faint clicking sound echoes.

choices.label: Convince Marcus to stay and fortify the rooftop
choices.description: You argue that the rooftop is defensible. You can see approaches from all sides. Maybe you should wait for daylight, or for military rescue. Marcus reluctantly agrees to wait—for now. You start gathering whatever you can use to fortify your position.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You and Marcus fortify the rooftop access as best you can. Hours pass. The city burns below you. Then, just before dawn, you hear it—helicopter blades. A military chopper sweeps low over the rooftops. Rescue might actually be coming. But so are more infected, drawn by the noise.

script.content: You ignore Marcus and move past him, scanning the rooftop's perimeter. He watches you with narrowed eyes but doesn't try to stop you. 'Suit yourself,' he mutters, turning back to his own planning.

You find what you're looking for: a thick drainage pipe running down the side of the building, bolted to the brick. Below, an alley snakes between buildings, shrouded in shadow. You can't see any infected in that immediate area.
The pipe is slick with moisture and grime. It'll be a dangerous climb, but it's a way down that doesn't involve trusting a stranger with a crowbar.
Alone is safer. Alone means I only have to watch my own back.

choices.label: Climb down the drainage pipe
choices.description: You grab the pipe and lower yourself over the edge. The cold metal is slippery, but you find footholds. You descend into the shadowy alley, leaving Marcus and the rooftop behind.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You land hard in the alley, your ankles jarring from the drop. You're at street level. The alley opens onto a side street. You can hear the distant moans of the infected. A convenience store at the end of the alley has its door smashed open—a potential source of supplies.

choices.label: Reconsider and call Marcus back
choices.description: Before you commit to the climb, you reconsider. Maybe going alone is suicide. You turn back to find Marcus—but he's already gone. The rooftop is empty. You're truly alone now, with only one way down.
choices.targetSceneDescription: Marcus has vanished—probably crossed to the next building without you. The rooftop access door below is beginning to shudder. Something is trying to break through from inside the building. The only way off the roof is down the drainage pipe. You have no choice now.

script.content: You help Marcus lay the plank across the gap between buildings. It wobbles precariously, settling with a scraping thud on the opposite ledge. Eight feet of empty air stretches below you.
I'll go first. Watch how I do it—slow, steady, arms out. Don't look at the alley. Look at me.
Marcus crosses with practiced ease, his boots finding the center of the plank. He jumps down on the other side and turns, offering a nod of encouragement.

You step onto the plank. Your heart is a drum in your chest. The wind tries to push you off balance. Below, in the alley, you hear the infected moaning, but they haven't seen you. Step by step, you make your way across. You jump down beside Marcus, legs shaking.

You've made it. The fire escape on this building leads down into a dark alley. Marcus leads you to a fire door at the rooftop's edge. Beyond it lies the interior of the office building—a dark maze of cubicles, shattered glass, and shadows.
Stay close. Keep quiet. We go down, find a vehicle, and head for the police station. You with me?

choices.label: Follow Marcus through the office building
choices.description: You stick with Marcus. Together, you descend into the dark office building, navigating by touch and the dim light from outside.
choices.targetSceneDescription: The office building is a labyrinth of cubicles and dark corridors. You follow Marcus past overturned desks and shattered computers. A faint clicking sound echoes ahead—rhythmic, like typing. But no one is at the computers. Something is tapping its fingernails against a desk in the darkness.

choices.label: Suggest finding a vehicle instead
choices.description: You ask Marcus if there's a garage or parking lot nearby. If you can find a working car, you could drive to the police station, avoiding the streets on foot.
choices.targetSceneDescription: Marcus nods and leads you down the fire escape to street level. A parking lot behind the building holds several cars. Most are damaged, but one—an old pickup truck—looks intact. The keys might still be inside. But the lot is open ground, and infected are shuffling in the nearby streets.

script.content: You grab the drainage pipe and lower yourself over the edge. The cold metal is slick with moisture, and your hands slip as you find footholds on the rusty bolts. You descend hand over hand, your arms burning with the effort.
Three stories down, your feet hit the ground hard. Pain lances through your ankles, but you're down. You press yourself against the wall, catching your breath.

The alley stretches before you, shrouded in shadow. At the far end, you can see a side street lit by the glow of burning cars. A convenience store at the mouth of the alley has its door smashed open—a potential source of supplies.
Between you and the store, two infected shuffle past the alley entrance, their heads swiveling erratically. They haven't seen you yet.

choices.label: Wait for the infected to pass, then search the store
choices.description: You press into the shadows and wait. The infected drift past. You slip into the convenience store. Inside, the shelves are half-stocked, but there's food, water, and a first-aid kit behind the counter.
choices.targetSceneDescription: The convenience store is a treasure trove. You grab bottled water, energy bars, a flashlight, batteries, and a small first-aid kit. As you're stuffing your backpack, you hear a vehicle engine outside. Someone is driving through the city. This could be rescue—or raiders.

choices.label: Sneak past the infected and follow the street
choices.description: You don't want to get trapped in a store. You slip out of the alley and move down the side street, keeping to the shadows of parked cars.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You move quickly through the burning streets, sticking to shadows and alleyways. You pass bodies and wreckage. After several blocks, you hear gunshots—not infected, but human. Someone else is alive out here, and they're fighting back.

script.content: Wait. We can hold this position. The door is the only way up, and we can barricade it. Come daylight, someone might come for us.
Marcus scowls but nods reluctantly. 'Alright. We try it your way. But if this goes sideways, we're doing it my way.'

Together, you drag HVAC units, furniture, and debris to block the rooftop access door. The night stretches on. You sit back-to-back with Marcus, watching the city burn, listening to the distant screams and howls. Hours pass. The stars are hidden by smoke.

Just before dawn, you hear it—the rhythmic thwump-thwump-thwump of helicopter blades. A military chopper sweeps low over the rooftops, a searchlight sweeping across the buildings. Hope surges in your chest.
They're here! We need to signal them!

But the chopper's noise is drawing attention. From the street below, a surge of infected begins to climb. They're scaling the walls, swarming the fire escape. The barricaded door begins to shudder as something heavy throws itself against it from below.

choices.label: Signal the helicopter and hold the roof
choices.description: You and Marcus wave frantically, light a fire with debris, do whatever it takes to catch the chopper's attention while fighting off the infected scaling the building.
choices.targetSceneDescription: The helicopter spots you. It swings around, blades thundering. A soldier leans out, waving you toward a landing zone. But the infected are pouring onto the rooftop now. You and Marcus fight back-to-back, buying time as the chopper descends. Rescue is seconds away—if you can hold.

choices.label: Abandon the rooftop and descend the fire escape
choices.description: The plan is failing. The infected are everywhere. You grab Marcus and pull him toward the fire escape. There's still time to go down and find cover in the building.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You and Marcus abandon the rooftop, descending into the dark office building below. The interior is a maze of cubicles and shadows. The helicopter's searchlight sweeps past the windows. Below, infected pound at the building's entrance. You're trapped between floors.

script.content: You turn back to call Marcus, but he's already gone. The rooftop is empty. He crossed without you.
Then you hear it—a heavy thud from below. The rooftop access door shudders. Something massive is throwing itself against it from the inside. The metal groans. A crack appears in the frame.

You have one way off this roof: the drainage pipe. You scramble to the edge and grab it, lowering yourself down as fast as you can. Behind you, the door explodes open and a howl of fury splits the night.

choices.label: Climb down the pipe quickly
choices.description: You descend the pipe in a controlled fall, your hands burning. You drop the last ten feet and hit the ground running.

choices.label: Try to cross the gap instead
choices.description: You change your mind and run for the plank Marcus left behind. It's still there. But you have no one to spot you, and the infected are pouring onto the roof.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You run across the plank in desperation. It wobbles dangerously. An infected lunges onto the plank behind you. You reach the other side and kick the plank away, sending the infected plummeting into the alley. You're alone on the other rooftop, with no way back.

script.content: You grab a lamp and smash it against the fire escape window. Glass explodes outward. The infected on the other side recoils briefly, giving you a split second to strike.

You lunge forward, driving your kitchen knife into the creature's chest. It doesn't even flinch. It grabs your arm with terrifying strength, its nails digging into your flesh. You scream and stab again—this time in the throat. Black blood gushes. The creature gurgles and falls back off the fire escape, taking your knife with it.
You stumble back, gasping. Blood runs down your arm where it clawed you. Three deep scratches. That's when you hear it—the front door finally gives way with a thunderous crack.
Mrs. Gutierrez screams. The infected are inside.

choices.label: Flee out the broken window with Mrs. Gutierrez
choices.description: You grab Mrs. Gutierrez and drag her toward the shattered window. The fire escape is your only way out now. You climb onto it, pulling her after you, as the infected swarm into your apartment behind you.

choices.label: Make a last stand with the lamp as a weapon
choices.description: Your knife is gone, but you still have the broken lamp. You grab a metal rod from it and face the infected pouring through the door. You'll sell your life dearly.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You stand your ground, swinging the metal rod. You take down two infected before they overwhelm you. Your last sight is Mrs. Gutierrez being cornered by the window. The world goes dark.

script.content: You pull Mrs. Gutierrez into the bedroom closet, sliding the door shut just as the front door splinters. You press your hand over her mouth, feeling her tears wet your fingers. She's trembling so hard you're afraid the sound will give you away.

Through the slats of the closet door, you watch shadows move across the bedroom. The infected shuffle past the closet, their breathing wet and labored. One pauses right outside the door. A long, agonizing moment. Then it moves on.
Minutes pass. The sounds of the infected fade. They've left the apartment, moving on to hunt elsewhere. You and Mrs. Gutierrez are alone in the dark, cramped closet. You survived—for now.
Oh God, oh thank God. What do we do now?

choices.label: Check the apartment and gather supplies
choices.description: You cautiously emerge from the closet. The apartment is trashed but empty. You grab whatever supplies you can find—food, water, a knife from the kitchen. You need to decide your next move.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You scavenge what you can from your ruined apartment. Mrs. Gutierrez follows you like a shadow. You have a choice: try to reach the ground floor through the now-empty hallway, or take the fire escape up to the rooftop and look for a way down from there.

choices.label: Stay hidden and wait for dawn
choices.description: It's too dangerous to move at night. You decide to stay in the closet until daylight. Mrs. Gutierrez eventually falls into an exhausted sleep. You keep watch, listening to the city's death throes.
choices.targetSceneDescription: Dawn breaks over a ruined city. You emerge from the closet stiff and hungry. The building is eerily quiet. From the window, you see the street below—wreckage, bodies, and smoke. But in the distance, you see movement. Survivors, maybe. A group of people making their way through the debris.

script.content: You haul Mrs. Gutierrez onto the rooftop just as the first infected reaches the top rung. You kick the ladder away with all your strength. It peels off the building and crashes into the alley below, taking the infected with it.
You collapse onto the tar-paper roof, gasping. Mrs. Gutierrez is sobbing quietly, clutching her torn nightgown. The wind whips across the rooftop, carrying the smell of smoke.
A shadow falls over you. You look up to see a man standing a few yards away, a crowbar in his hand. He's been watching you. It's Marcus from the second floor.
Well, well. Looks like you made it. Brought company, I see.
Please, you have to help us. There's more of them. They're everywhere.

choices.label: Trust Marcus and work together
choices.description: Marcus seems capable and level-headed. The three of you might have a better chance together. You suggest pooling resources and finding a way off the rooftop.

choices.label: Keep your distance from Marcus
choices.description: You don't know this man. You thank him for the moment but make it clear you'll go your own way. You take Mrs. Gutierrez to the far side of the rooftop, looking for another way down.

choices.label: Ask Marcus what he knows about the situation
choices.description: Marcus has been up here longer than you. He might know what's happening, where the safe zones are, or how to escape the city.

script.content: You step through the shattered glass of the pharmacy entrance, your shoes crunching on the debris. The interior is dark, lit only by the distant glow of fires outside. The smell of medicine and decay hangs heavy in the air.

A figure hunches over by the prescription counter—an infected, its face buried in the remains of what was once a person. It makes wet, slobbering sounds that turn your stomach. It hasn't noticed you yet.
Behind the counter, you can see shelves stocked with supplies—antibiotics, bandages, painkillers. A survivor's goldmine. But the infected is right there.

choices.label: Try to sneak past the infected to get supplies
choices.description: You hold your breath and creep along the wall, keeping low behind the shelves. The infected is distracted by its meal. If you're careful, you can grab what you need and slip out unnoticed.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You manage to slip past the feeding infected and grab a backpack full of medical supplies. As you're about to leave, you knock over a bottle. The infected spins around with a shriek. You bolt for the exit, crashing through the broken window back onto the street.

choices.label: Kill the infected silently
choices.description: You need those supplies, and you can't risk the infected raising an alarm. You grip your weapon and approach the creature from behind, aiming for the base of its skull.
choices.targetSceneDescription: Your strike is true. The infected drops without a sound. You quickly gather supplies—bandages, antiseptic, painkillers, antibiotics. As you're stuffing them into your bag, you hear heavy footsteps outside. A group of infected is passing by the pharmacy entrance.

script.content: You move through the burning streets like a ghost, keeping to shadows, ducking behind overturned cars when you hear shuffling footsteps. The city is a nightmare of fire, smoke, and distant screams.
After several blocks, you hear gunshots—close, maybe two blocks away. Not the random discharge of a panicked civilian, but controlled, rhythmic shots. Military? Police?

You edge toward the sound, peering around a corner. You see a barricaded intersection. Sandbags, a burned-out police cruiser, and armed figures in makeshift armor. Survivors have fortified a position.
But between you and the barricade, a horde of infected mills about, drawn by the gunfire. Dozens of them. They haven't seen you yet.

choices.label: Try to reach the barricade
choices.description: Safety is right there. If you can find a way through or around the horde, you could reach the survivors. You scan the area for an alternate route.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You find a drainage culvert that runs under the street. It's dark, wet, and cramped, but it leads past the horde. You crawl through filth and darkness, emerging on the other side. The barricade is twenty yards away. The survivors spot you and wave you in.

choices.label: Find another way
choices.description: The barricade is too dangerous a gamble. You turn away and continue down a side street, looking for a less fortified but safer path out of the city.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You take a side street that leads to a residential neighborhood. The fires are less intense here. You find an abandoned bicycle and a map. The highway is two miles east. If you can reach it, you might find military convoys or fleeing survivors.

script.content: You scream and lunge at the nearest infected, driving your kitchen knife forward with all the desperate strength you can muster. The blade sinks into its eye socket. Black fluid sprays. The creature convulses and collapses.

But the second infected is already on you. It tackles you down the concrete stairs. Pain explodes through your back and shoulder as you tumble, landing in a heap on the ground floor landing. The creature is on top of you, snapping its jaws inches from your face.
You grapple with the creature, its rotting breath washing over you. Your hand closes on something—a shard of broken glass from a smashed window. You drive it into the side of its head. It goes limp.

You push the body off you, gasping, covered in black blood and your own. You're wounded—your back screams with pain, and you might have broken ribs. But you're alive. The exit door is right there. Beyond it: the street.

choices.label: Push through the exit to the street
choices.description: You stagger through the exit door, emerging onto a side street. The street is relatively quiet. You need to find shelter, medical supplies, and a plan.

choices.label: Check the basement level for a safer route
choices.description: Instead of going outside, you descend further into the building's basement. There might be a parking garage or maintenance tunnels that offer a safer path through the city.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You descend into the basement. It's pitch black. You find a maintenance tunnel that connects to neighboring buildings—a hidden path through the city's underbelly. But in the darkness, you hear whispers. Not infected. Something else.

script.content: You and Marcus descend into the dark office building. The interior is a maze of cubicles, overturned desks, and shattered computer monitors. Emergency lights cast dim red shadows across the space.
A faint clicking sound echoes ahead—rhythmic, like fingernails tapping on a desk. But no one is at the computers. The sound comes from deeper in the darkness.
You hearing that? It's not infected. Infected don't tap—they just... scream and bite.

choices.label: Investigate the clicking sound with Marcus
choices.description: The sound might be another survivor. You and Marcus creep toward the source, weapons ready.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You find a security guard named Delroy hiding in a janitor's closet, tapping his fingernails nervously against a metal shelf. He's terrified but unharmed. He has keys, a flashlight, and knowledge of the building's layout. He says there's an underground parking garage with a service exit nearby.

choices.label: Head straight for the stairwell
choices.description: You can't risk unknown threats. You suggest to Marcus that you find the emergency stairwell and head down directly.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You and Marcus find the emergency stairwell. It's clear for now. You descend floor by floor. On the second floor landing, you hear voices below—human voices. A group of survivors is in the lobby, arguing.

script.content: Marcus leads you down the fire escape to street level. A parking lot behind the building holds several cars—most are damaged, windshields smashed, tires slashed. But one vehicle catches your eye: an old pickup truck sitting alone in the corner.
Nearby, a sport motorcycle lies on its side. The keys are still in the ignition. Both are options.
We take the truck, we can carry more. We take the bike, we're faster. Your call.

choices.label: Take the pickup truck
choices.description: The truck is sturdy and can carry supplies. You approach carefully. The keys are in the visor. The engine turns over with a roar.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You're in a stolen pickup truck, careening through ruined streets. Infected scatter as you barrel past. Marcus navigates from the passenger seat. You're heading for the police station, but the road ahead is blocked by a collapsed overpass.

choices.label: Take the motorcycle instead
choices.description: The motorcycle is faster and more maneuverable. You right the bike and kick-start it. Marcus climbs on behind you.
choices.targetSceneDescription: The motorcycle weaves through alleys and side streets that a car couldn't fit. You feel exposed, but you're making good time toward the highway. Then you hear it—a massive crash ahead, and the roar of something bigger than infected.

script.content: The convenience store is a treasure trove. Shelves are still stocked—the looters haven't gotten here yet. You grab bottled water, energy bars, batteries, a flashlight, and a small first-aid kit from behind the counter.

As you're stuffing your backpack, you hear it—a vehicle engine. Tires crunching on debris. You peer through the shattered front window and see a pickup truck rolling slowly down the street, its bed full of armed people.
They look like survivors, not raiders. They're scanning the buildings, clearly looking for supplies or other survivors.

choices.label: Try to flag down the vehicle
choices.description: You step out and wave. The truck screeches to a halt. Armed survivors stare at you. 'You bit?' the driver asks. You prove you're clean.
choices.targetSceneDescription: The survivors in the truck are heading to a refugee camp set up at the city stadium. They offer you a ride. The truck bed is crowded but safe—for now.

choices.label: Avoid the vehicle and go solo
choices.description: You don't know these people. You grab what you can and slip out the back, disappearing into the alley network.

script.content: The helicopter swings back toward your rooftop, its searchlight bathing you in blinding light. The rotors create a hurricane of wind and noise. A soldier leans out, motioning frantically.
But the noise has drawn every infected for blocks. They pour onto the rooftop—climbing over the edges, breaking through the door. The barricade crumbles.

choices.label: Run for the rope ladder
choices.description: You sprint toward the descending rope ladder as the helicopter hovers. Infected close in from all sides. It's a desperate dash for survival.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You grab the rope ladder as the helicopter begins to ascend. Infected grab at your legs. You kick them off and haul yourself up. Looking down, you see Marcus fighting alone on the rooftop, surrounded. You reach for him, but the helicopter is already climbing.

choices.label: Fight back-to-back with Marcus
choices.description: You and Marcus stand together, swinging your weapons, covering each other as the helicopter descends to land. It's risky—it gives the infected time to surround you—but it keeps you both alive.
choices.targetSceneDescription: The helicopter touches down. You and Marcus fight your way to the open door. Soldiers pull you aboard. The chopper lifts off as infected swarm the landing skids. You made it. Both of you. The city shrinks below as you fly toward safety.

script.content: You run for the plank, your heart hammering. Behind you, the infected swarm onto the rooftop—dozens of them, pouring through the shattered door. They see you. They charge.
The plank stretches across the gap, eight feet of wooden hope. Below, a three-story drop into darkness.
You have a split second to decide.

choices.label: Sprint across the plank
choices.description: You take a deep breath and sprint across the plank. It wobbles wildly beneath you. An infected lunges onto the plank behind you, scrambling forward.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You reach the other side and kick the plank away, sending the creature plummeting. But you're on the wrong rooftop now—farther from safety, with no way back. You need to find a new way down, and the infected are watching from across the gap.

choices.label: Abandon the plank and go down the pipe
choices.description: The plank is too risky. You dive for the drainage pipe instead, sliding down it in a controlled fall, hitting the ground hard and rolling to your feet.

script.content: You grab the jagged metal rod from the shattered lamp and face the door. The infected pour through—not one, not two, but a flood of twisted bodies. You swing, connecting with the first one's skull. It drops. A second takes its place.

You fight with everything you have. You take down three, four of them. But there are too many. They drag you down, their claws tearing, their teeth finding purchase. Mrs. Gutierrez's scream is the last thing you hear before the world goes dark.
Your story ends here, in your own apartment, surrounded by the monsters the world has become.
You emerge from the closet, heart pounding. The apartment is destroyed—furniture overturned, drawers pulled out, your belongings scattered. But the infected are gone.

You move quickly, grabbing what you can: a kitchen knife, a flashlight that still works, a half-full water bottle, some granola bars. Mrs. Gutierrez finds a heavy frying pan and clutches it like a lifeline.
What now? Where do we go?

choices.label: Take the hallway to the ground floor
choices.description: The hallway is clear now. You and Mrs. Gutierrez creep toward the stairwell, hoping the infected have moved on to other hunting grounds.
choices.targetSceneDescription: The stairwell is empty, stained with blood and violence. You descend carefully, Mrs. Gutierrez following close behind. The ground floor lobby is a wreck, but the front doors are open. Outside, the street is eerily quiet.

choices.label: Head up to the rooftop via fire escape
choices.description: Going down means risking more infected. You decide to go up to the rooftop and see if there's a better view of the situation—or a way to signal for help.

script.content: Dawn creeps through the closet's slats, pale and gray. You've survived the night. Your legs are cramped, your mouth dry, but you're alive.

You emerge from the closet stiff and hungry. Mrs. Gutierrez follows, her eyes red from crying. Through the apartment window, you see the city in daylight for the first time since it fell. Smoke rises from a dozen fires. Wreckage litters the streets. But in the distance, you see movement—figures picking their way through the debris.
Survivors. They're heading east, away from the worst of the fires. You could try to catch up to them.

choices.label: Follow the survivors east
choices.description: There's safety in numbers. You and Mrs. Gutierrez gather your meager supplies and head out, trying to catch up to the group in the distance.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You follow the group at a distance, keeping to cover. They lead you through back alleys and side streets, avoiding main roads. After an hour, you reach a makeshift checkpoint—a survivor encampment at a school. Armed men and women watch the perimeter.

choices.label: Search for supplies first, then head out
choices.description: You can't travel without more supplies. You check neighboring apartments for food, water, and medicine before attempting the journey.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You search the other apartments on your floor. Most are empty or ransacked. In apartment 3A, you find canned food, a medical kit, and a radio. The radio crackles with a recorded message: 'Survivors report to the stadium. Military evacuation in progress.'

script.content: You hold your breath and creep along the wall, keeping low behind the pharmacy shelves. The infected is distracted, making wet sounds as it feeds. Your hand finds bandages, antiseptic wipes, and a bottle of painkillers. You stuff them into your bag.

You reach for a box of antibiotics on the top shelf. Your fingers brush it—and it falls. The bottle clatters on the linoleum floor. The infected's head snaps up. Its black eyes lock onto you. It screeches.

You bolt for the exit, crashing through the broken window and landing hard on the sidewalk. Behind you, the infected scrambles through the glass after you. You run, ignoring the burning in your lungs.

choices.label: Keep running and lose it in the alleys
choices.description: You duck into a maze of alleys, leaping over trash and debris. The infected gives chase but you're faster, more desperate. You lose it after several blocks.

choices.label: Turn and fight
choices.description: You can't outrun everything. You stop, spin, and raise your weapon. The infected lunges. You sidestep and bring your weapon down on its skull.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You take down the infected with a well-aimed strike. Panting, you look around. The street is empty. You have medical supplies, but you're exhausted and exposed. A distant siren wails.

script.content: You approach the infected from behind, your weapon raised. Your hand trembles. One clean strike—that's all it takes. You bring the blade down at the base of its skull.

The creature crumples without a sound. You stand over it, breathing hard, staring at what you've done. It was a person once. Maybe someone's father, someone's brother. But you don't have time for that now.

You gather supplies quickly—antibiotics, bandages, painkillers, antiseptic. As you're stuffing them into your bag, you hear heavy footsteps outside. A group of infected is passing by the pharmacy entrance.

choices.label: Hide behind the counter until they pass
choices.description: You duck behind the prescription counter, clutching your bag of supplies. The infected shuffle past the pharmacy entrance, their guttural moans fading as they move on.
choices.targetSceneDescription: The infected pass. You emerge from hiding. You're alive, armed with medical supplies, and alone. The street outside is empty now. You can hear distant gunfire to the east. People are still fighting.

choices.label: Try to slip out the back
choices.description: There might be a back exit. You search the pharmacy's rear and find a stockroom door leading to an alley. You slip out quietly.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You emerge into a narrow alley behind the pharmacy. A chain-link fence blocks one end, but the other leads to a side street. As you move toward the street, you see a man in a leather jacket crouched behind a dumpster—Marcus.

script.content: You spot a drainage culvert that runs under the street—a dark, narrow tunnel that leads past the horde. It's filled with filthy water and God knows what else, but it's your only path.
You lower yourself into the culvert. The water is freezing cold and rises to your chest. You wade through the darkness, your hand on the slimy wall, trying not to think about what you're touching.
You emerge on the other side, dripping and shivering. The barricade is twenty yards away. A survivor spots you and shouts. Hands wave you in. You run.
You scramble over the sandbags and collapse inside the perimeter. Rough hands pat you down for bites, check you for fever. You're in. You've found a safe zone—for now.

choices.label: Tell the survivors what you've seen
choices.description: You share information about the building you came from, the infected activity, and the general state of the streets. The survivors are grateful for the intel.
choices.targetSceneDescription: The survivors welcome your information. Their leader, a former police officer named Rivera, explains that they're trying to hold this intersection as a checkpoint for evacuees. They have radios, and they've heard the military is evacuating people from the stadium downtown.

choices.label: Rest and recover before deciding your next move
choices.description: You're exhausted, cold, and hungry. You ask for a moment to rest. Someone hands you a blanket and a cup of water. You sit against a sandbag and close your eyes, just for a moment.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You rest at the barricade for an hour. When you wake, the situation has changed—the horde has moved on, but more survivors have trickled in with news of a military evacuation at the football stadium, three miles east.

script.content: You turn away from the barricade and head down a quieter side street. The residential neighborhood is eerily peaceful compared to the chaos behind you. Lawns are overgrown, mail sits in boxes, and a child's bicycle lies abandoned on a driveway.
You find an abandoned bicycle leaning against a fence. The tires are good. A map is tucked into the basket. The highway is marked two miles east.
You pedal through the quiet streets, the only sound the whir of wheels on asphalt. It feels almost normal—until you round a corner and see a military checkpoint ahead. Real soldiers, with real guns.

choices.label: Approach the military checkpoint
choices.description: The soldiers see you. They raise their weapons but don't fire. You raise your hands. 'I'm not infected!' you shout. They motion you forward for screening.
choices.targetSceneDescription: The soldiers are from the National Guard. They've set up an evacuation point. They screen you for bites and fever, then wave you toward a waiting bus. 'We're taking survivors to the stadium. Safe zone's there.'

choices.label: Avoid the checkpoint and keep going on your own
choices.description: You don't trust the military. You've seen too many movies where the safe zone is just another trap. You veer away and continue east on your own.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You bypass the checkpoint and continue toward the highway. The road is clogged with abandoned cars. You weave between them on your bike. In the distance, you see columns of smoke rising from what might be the stadium.

script.content: You descend into the basement. The air grows cold and damp. Emergency lights flicker, casting long shadows across concrete walls. You find a service door marked 'MAINTENANCE TUNNEL.'

The tunnel stretches into darkness, connecting to neighboring buildings. It's a hidden path through the city's underbelly—safe from the infected above. But as you move deeper, you hear whispers. Faint, echoing voices.
The whispers grow louder. You round a corner and see them—a group of survivors huddled around a small fire in a junction of tunnels. They see you. Hands reach for weapons.
Whoa there! Who are you? You bit?

choices.label: Prove you're clean and join the tunnel survivors
choices.description: You show them your arms, let them check you. They relax slightly. Their leader, a woman named Rosa, explains they've been living in the tunnels since the outbreak. They know a safe route to the city outskirts.
choices.targetSceneDescription: Rosa and her group have built a small community in the tunnels. They have food, water, and a plan to escape the city through an old storm drain that leads beyond the quarantine zone. They offer you a place among them.

choices.label: Back away and find another route
choices.description: You don't trust anyone down here. You raise your hands and slowly back away, disappearing back into the dark tunnel.
choices.targetSceneDescription: You retreat into the darkness, navigating the tunnels alone. After an hour of wandering, you find a ladder leading up to a manhole cover. You push it open and climb out onto an empty street on the edge of the city.

choices.description: You and Marcus find a terrified security guard named Delroy hiding in a janitor's closet. He has keys and knows the building. He leads you to the underground parking garage, where a service vehicle is still operational.
choices.label: Trust Delroy and follow his lead
choices.targetSceneDescription: Delroy leads you through the parking garage. You find a maintenance van with keys inside. As you drive toward the exit ramp, you see the garage entrance is blocked by a collapsed concrete barrier. You'll have to find another way out—or clear the rubble.

choices.description: You thank Delroy for the information but decide to split up—three people moving together make too much noise. You take the stairs alone.
choices.label: Take the stairs alone

script.content: The clicking leads you to a janitor's closet. You open it to find a man in a security uniform huddled in the corner, tapping his fingernails nervously against a metal shelf. He nearly screams when he sees you.
Don't shoot! Don't hurt me! I'm not one of them!
Easy, easy. We're not infected. We're from the building next door. What's your name?
Delroy. I'm the night security guard. When everything went to hell, I locked myself in here. I've been listening to them out there... shuffling, scratching...

Delroy has a ring of keys, a heavy flashlight, and knowledge of the building. He says there's a service elevator to the underground parking garage, and from there a maintenance exit to the next block.

choices.description: You descend to the lobby and approach the group of survivors. They're arguing about whether to stay or try to reach the stadium. One of them, a woman with a shotgun, notices you first.
choices.label: Join the lobby survivors
choices.targetSceneDescription: The lobby survivors are a mixed group—office workers, a janitor, two security guards. They've barricaded the entrances but know they can't hold out forever. They're debating whether to make a run for the stadium. They could use another able body.

choices.description: You signal Marcus to stay quiet. You don't know these people. You slip past the lobby and find the service exit to the alley.
choices.label: Sneak past the lobby
choices.targetSceneDescription: You and Marcus slip out a service door into an alley. You emerge on a side street near a convenience store. In the distance, you see a pickup truck full of armed survivors rolling slowly down the main road.

script.content: You find the emergency stairwell. The door opens onto a concrete staircase descending into darkness. The air is cool and still. No sounds of infected—for now.
You descend floor by floor. On the second floor landing, you hear voices below. Human voices. A heated argument echoes up the stairwell.
—can't stay here! They'll find us eventually!
And go where? The streets are crawling with those things!

choices.description: The truck is tough. You crash through the blockade of abandoned cars, bouncing onto the sidewalk, then find a side street that loops around the overpass collapse. You're gaining ground on the police station.
choices.label: Crash through the blockade
choices.targetSceneDescription: You ram the pickup through a collapsed fence and find an alternate route. The police station appears ahead, its parking lot fortified with sandbags. Armed officers wave you in. You've found an official safe zone.

choices.description: The overpass collapse is a sign. You turn around and head for the highway entrance ramp instead, hoping to get out of the city entirely.
choices.label: Turn around and head for the highway

script.content: The truck's engine roars to life, shattering the relative quiet. Infected in the nearby streets turn toward the sound, their heads snapping around with that terrible, synchronized motion.
Go! Go! Go!
You floor it. The truck lurches forward, crashing through a chain-link fence and onto the main road. Infected scatter as you barrel past. You grip the wheel, your knuckles white.
You're heading for the police station, but as you round a corner, you see it—a collapsed overpass blocking the road ahead. Concrete slabs and twisted rebar create an impassable wall.

choices.description: The open road stretches ahead. You twist the throttle and the bike surges forward. You weave through abandoned cars, feeling the wind. For a moment, you feel almost free.
choices.label: Ride for the highway
choices.targetSceneDescription: The motorcycle eats up the miles. You reach the highway on-ramp. Ahead, the road is clogged with abandoned vehicles, but there's a path through. In the distance, you see military helicopters in the sky.

choices.description: You hear a massive crash ahead and brake hard. Something big is coming. You veer into a parking garage to take cover and reassess.
choices.label: Take cover in a parking garage
choices.targetSceneDescription: You duck into a multi-story parking garage. The engine echoes off concrete walls. Above you, levels of parked cars stretch into darkness. From the upper levels, you hear a scraping sound—something being dragged across concrete.

script.content: You right the motorcycle and swing your leg over. Marcus climbs on behind you. The bike starts with a satisfying growl. You twist the throttle and pull out of the parking lot.

The motorcycle weaves through alleys and side streets that a car couldn't fit. You feel exposed, vulnerable, but you're making good time. The wind whips past as you navigate around debris and abandoned vehicles.
Then you hear it—a massive crash ahead, followed by the roar of something bigger than infected. A building facade collapses into the street ahead, sending up a cloud of dust and debris.

choices.description: You climb into the truck bed. The survivors are heading to the stadium refugee camp. The ride is rough, but you feel safer in a group.
choices.label: Ride with them to the stadium
choices.targetSceneDescription: The truck rumbles through the ruined streets toward the stadium. The camp is a sprawling tent city surrounded by military vehicles. Thousands of survivors huddle within the fences. You've found civilization—but the camp is overcrowded and tensions are high.

choices.description: You thank them but decline. You prefer to travel alone. They shrug and drive off. You watch them go, wondering if you made the right choice.
choices.label: Decline and go solo

script.content: You step out of the convenience store, hands raised. The pickup truck screeches to a halt. Two armed men and a woman level their weapons at you.
You bit? Show me your arms!
You roll up your sleeves, showing clean skin. The driver, a grizzled man with a scar across his cheek, nods slowly.
Get in. We're heading to the stadium. They've set up a refugee camp there. Military's running it.

choices.description: You grab the rope ladder and start climbing as the helicopter ascends. Infected grab at your legs, but you kick them off. You pull yourself up, gasping. Below, Marcus is surrounded.
choices.label: Reach for Marcus from the ladder
choices.targetSceneDescription: You cling to the rope ladder, reaching down for Marcus. He makes a desperate leap and grabs your hand. The helicopter climbs higher. You haul him up as infected snatch at the air below. You both make it, dangling from the ladder as the city falls away beneath you.

choices.description: You scramble up the rope, not looking back. Marcus was a useful ally, but you can't die for him. You climb into the helicopter and collapse on the floor.
choices.label: Save yourself
choices.targetSceneDescription: You're pulled into the helicopter. Below, Marcus disappears under a wave of infected. The soldier closes the door. You close your eyes. You survived. But the look the soldier gives you says everything.

script.content: You sprint for the rope ladder as it descends from the hovering helicopter. The rotor wash batters you, threatening to knock you off your feet. Behind you, infected claw their way across the rooftop.
You grab the rope. It swings wildly. Below you, an infected lunges—its fingers brush your ankle. You kick out, feeling its jaw break. You start to climb.
Looking down, you see Marcus fighting alone on the rooftop, his crowbar swinging. He's holding them back, giving you time. But he's being surrounded.

choices.description: The helicopter touches down. You and Marcus fight your way to the open door as soldiers cover you. You're both pulled aboard as the chopper lifts off, leaving the infected behind.
choices.label: Both of you make it
choices.targetSceneDescription: You and Marcus sit on the vibrating floor of the helicopter, gasping, bleeding, but alive. A medic checks your wounds. Below, the city burns. You're heading to a military base outside the city. You made it. You both made it.

choices.description: At the last second, Marcus shoves you toward the helicopter and turns to face the horde. 'Go!' he roars. 'I'll hold them off!'
choices.label: Marcus sacrifices himself
choices.targetSceneDescription: You're dragged into the helicopter as Marcus throws himself at the advancing infected, buying you precious seconds. The last image you see is him swinging his crowbar, disappearing beneath a sea of bodies.

script.content: The helicopter touches down on the rooftop, its skids barely finding purchase on the tar-paper surface. A soldier leans out, screaming over the rotor noise, 'GET IN! NOW!'

You and Marcus fight back-to-back, a whirlwind of crowbar and pipe. An infected charges—you smash its skull. Another lunges—Marcus's crowbar takes it in the throat. You're a team, moving in perfect sync.
You reach the helicopter door. Soldiers grab your arms and haul you inside. Marcus is right behind you. An infected grabs his leg as he reaches for the door.

choices.description: You find a maintenance ladder on the side of the building. Climbing down, you emerge onto a quiet street.
choices.label: Climb down the maintenance ladder

choices.description: You spot a broken window on the top floor of this building. Inside, you might find supplies or another way down.
choices.label: Enter through a broken window
choices.targetSceneDescription: You climb through a broken window into a ransacked apartment. You find a working radio. A voice crackles: '...stadium... evacuation... repeat... military evacuation at the football stadium...'

script.content: You land hard on the opposite rooftop, roll, and scramble to your feet. The plank wobbles behind you. An infected lunges onto it, but you kick it away before it can cross. It plummets into the alley below with a wet crunch.
You're alone on an unfamiliar rooftop. Across the gap, the infected that pursued you mill about, unable to cross. For now, you're safe. But you need to find a way down.

choices.description: The staircase is clear. You and Mrs. Gutierrez descend carefully, making it to the ground floor. The lobby is destroyed, but the front doors are open. You step out onto the street.
choices.label: Exit onto the street

choices.description: You spot a basement door. Maybe there's another way out—or a place to hide.
choices.label: Check the basement

script.content: You open the front door of your apartment. The hallway is empty, lit only by the flickering emergency lights. The air is still.
Mrs. Gutierrez follows close behind, clutching her frying pan like a lifeline. You creep toward the stairwell. The door groans as you push it open.
The stairwell is empty. Blood stains the walls, but the infected are gone. You descend floor by floor, holding your breath at every landing.
You reach the ground floor. The lobby doors are open to the street. Outside, the world has changed forever.

choices.description: You hike through the damaged streets, following the trail of other survivors. The road to the stadium is littered with obstacles, but you push through. After two hours, the massive structure looms ahead, surrounded by military vehicles.
choices.label: Walk to the stadium
choices.targetSceneDescription: You arrive at the stadium refugee camp. Thousands of survivors are packed into the structure and surrounding tents. Soldiers patrol the perimeter. It's crowded, chaotic, but safe—for now. You've found sanctuary.

choices.description: You find a working bicycle and pedal toward the stadium, making better time. The wind in your face feels like freedom.
choices.label: Find a bicycle

script.content: You and Mrs. Gutierrez leave the apartment building, stepping into the daylight for the first time since the world ended. The street is a graveyard of cars and debris. Smoke hangs in the air like fog.

You spot the group of survivors ahead—maybe a dozen people moving single file along the side of the road. They're heading east, away from the worst of the fires. You follow at a distance, keeping to cover.

The trail leads through back alleys and side streets. After an hour, you see what they're heading toward: a massive structure rising above the low buildings. The football stadium. And around it, military vehicles.
Is that... rescue?

choices.description: You find canned food, bottled water, and a first-aid kit in apartment 3A. More importantly, you find a handgun in a nightstand drawer, with a box of ammunition. Mrs. Gutierrez looks at it with fear, but you feel safer.
choices.label: Take the gun and supplies
choices.targetSceneDescription: Armed and supplied, you're ready to face the city. You and Mrs. Gutierrez head for the stairwell, determined to reach the stadium where rescue awaits.

choices.description: You find a radio and manage to get a signal. A recorded message loops: 'Survivors report to the football stadium. Military evacuation in progress. Repeat: all survivors report to the stadium.'
choices.label: Listen to the radio message
choices.targetSceneDescription: The radio message gives you hope. The stadium is where you need to go. You pack what you can and set out, Mrs. Gutierrez at your side, heading toward the distant structure visible above the rooftops.

script.content: You step into the hallway, checking neighboring apartments. Most doors are open, the rooms ransacked. But apartment 3A is locked from the inside.
Mrs. Chen lives here. She's... she was my bridge partner.

You try the door. It's unlocked. You push it open slowly. The apartment is empty, but there are signs of a hurried departure. In the kitchen, you find canned food. In the bedroom, a first-aid kit. And in a nightstand drawer—a handgun.

choices.description: You catch your breath and check your supplies. The street ahead is clear. You decide to head east, following the sound of distant gunfire—where there's fighting, there are survivors.
choices.label: Head toward the gunfire

choices.description: You duck into a nearby building to rest and regroup. Any port in a storm.
choices.label: Take shelter in a building

script.content: You stop running. You turn. The infected lunges. You sidestep, using its momentum against it, and bring your weapon down on the base of its skull with all your strength.
It crumples. You stand over it, panting, your hands shaking. You did it. You won.
You check your bag. The medical supplies are still there. You're bleeding from a dozen small cuts from the pharmacy window, but nothing serious. You need to keep moving.

choices.description: The infected pass. You emerge from behind the counter, grab your supplies, and slip out onto the street. The coast is clear—for now.
choices.label: Head to the street

choices.description: You find a back door leading to an alley. You slip out, avoiding the street entirely.
choices.label: Exit through the back

script.content: You duck behind the prescription counter, pressing yourself into the shadows. Your heart hammers so loud you're sure it'll give you away.
The infected shuffle past the pharmacy entrance. You count their footsteps—six, maybe seven of them. One pauses at the door, letting out a low, guttural moan. Then it moves on.
The sounds fade. You're alone. You have a bag full of medical supplies and a clear path out.

choices.description: You emerge from the alley onto a side street. The neighborhood is quiet. You need to find a way to the stadium or the highway.
choices.label: Head toward the stadium

choices.description: You spot a military checkpoint in the distance. Soldiers are screening survivors. This could be your ticket out.
choices.label: Approach the military checkpoint

script.content: You slip into the alley, away from the main road. The shadows wrap around you like a blanket. The alley is narrow, cluttered with dumpsters and debris.
You pick your way through the trash, emerging at the far end onto a side street. The street is eerily quiet—no infected in sight. A few cars are abandoned, their doors hanging open.
In the distance, you can see the stadium rising above the low buildings. Smoke billows from somewhere nearby. The city holds its breath.

choices.description: You take the information about the barricade and the horde movements. Rivera radios ahead to warn others. You feel like you've made a difference.
choices.label: Share what you know
choices.targetSceneDescription: Rivera organizes a group to move toward the stadium. You travel with the barricade survivors, sharing your knowledge of the area. The journey is dangerous, but together you make it.

choices.description: You decide to stay at the barricade and help defend it. It may not be the stadium, but it's home now.
choices.label: Stay and defend the barricade

script.content: You sit down with Rivera, the barricade's leader. He's a weathered police officer in his fifties, his eyes carrying the weight of everything he's seen.
Tell me what you saw out there. Where'd you come from? How bad is it?
You describe the apartment building, the infected in the stairwell, the chaos in the streets. Rivera listens intently, nodding.
Good intel. We've been hearing reports that the military is setting up evacuation at the football stadium. We're planning to make a run for it. You in?

choices.description: You wake up to find the horde has moved on. More survivors have trickled in. The leader, Rivera, approaches you with news: 'The military is evacuating people from the stadium. We're going to make a run for it. You in?'
choices.label: Join the run to the stadium
choices.targetSceneDescription: You join a group of survivors making their way to the stadium. The journey is three miles through infected territory. But the group is armed and determined. Together, you might make it.

choices.description: You thank Rivera but decide to stay at the barricade. It's safer here. Maybe the military will come to you.
choices.label: Stay at the barricade
choices.targetSceneDescription: You stay at the barricade. Days pass. The infected grow bolder. Supplies run low. One night, the barricade falls. You make your last stand with the people who took you in. It's a good way to go.

script.content: You accept the blanket and cup of water gratefully. You find a spot against a sandbag and close your eyes, just for a moment. The sounds of the city fade into a dull backdrop.
You wake with a jolt. An hour has passed. The sun is higher now. Around you, the barricade is bustling with activity—more survivors have arrived, and the mood has shifted.
Good, you're awake. Listen—the horde moved on, but we've been hearing reports. Military evacuation at the football stadium. We're putting together a group to try to reach it.

choices.description: You pass the screening. A soldier directs you to a bus. 'We're taking everyone to the stadium. Safe zone's there.'
choices.label: Board the bus to the stadium

choices.description: The soldiers are overwhelmed—there are too many survivors and too few resources. You decide to slip away before they process you, keeping your freedom.
choices.label: Slip away before processing

script.content: You approach the checkpoint with your hands raised. Soldiers in full combat gear train their weapons on you.
Stop right there! Show me your arms! Any bites? Any scratches?
You comply. A soldier steps forward, checking you thoroughly. Satisfied, he nods to his comrades.
You're clean. Get on the bus. We're evacuating everyone to the stadium. It's the only safe zone left in the city.
You see a line of school buses idling behind the barricade. Survivors are being loaded onto them. Hope, fragile and real, flickers in your chest.

choices.description: The highway is clogged with abandoned cars, but you weave through them. In the distance, you see the city limits—and beyond them, open road. Freedom.
choices.label: Continue on the highway
choices.targetSceneDescription: You escape the city on the highway. The outbreak fades in your rearview mirror. You're alive. You're free. But the world beyond is unknown, and survival is a new kind of challenge.

choices.description: You spot a convoy of military vehicles heading toward the city. They're heading in the opposite direction. You flag them down.
choices.label: Flag down the military convoy
choices.targetSceneDescription: The convoy stops. Soldiers shout questions. You're screened and loaded onto a troop transport. They're heading to the stadium to reinforce the evacuation. You're going back into the city, but with an army at your back.

script.content: You reach the highway on-ramp. The road ahead is a parking lot of abandoned vehicles—cars, trucks, buses, all stopped in place, their doors hanging open like silent screams.
You weave between the stalled vehicles. Some still have their headlights on, batteries dying. A radio in one of the cars crackles with static.
In the distance, you see the edge of the city—the skyline giving way to open sky. Freedom is out there. But so is the unknown.

choices.description: The group welcomes you. Rosa, their leader, offers you a spot in their tunnel community. They have food, water, and a plan to escape through an old storm drain.
choices.label: Join the tunnel community
choices.targetSceneDescription: You join Rosa's group. They've been surviving in the tunnels for weeks. They know every passage, every junction. Their escape route leads to an old drainage system that empties into a river beyond the quarantine zone. Freedom awaits—if you can make it through the tunnels.

choices.description: You politely decline and ask if they can point you toward the surface exit instead.
choices.label: Ask for directions and leave

script.content: You hold your ground and show them your arms. Clean. No bites. The tension eases slightly. A woman with short gray hair and kind eyes steps forward.
Rosa. I'm the one keeping these folks alive down here. You lost?
You explain your situation. Rosa listens, nodding. Around her, the tunnel survivors watch you with wary eyes—men, women, even a few children. They've made a life down here in the darkness.

We've been down here since Day One. The infected don't come into the tunnels—too dark, too cold. We've got food, water, and a plan. There's an old storm drain that leads beyond the quarantine zone. We're leaving tonight. You can join us.

choices.description: You navigate the dark tunnels alone, following the flow of water. After an hour, you find a ladder leading up to a manhole cover. You push it open and climb out onto a street on the edge of the city.
choices.label: Exit the city through the tunnels
choices.targetSceneDescription: You emerge from the tunnels on the outskirts of the city. The air is cleaner here. The sounds of chaos are distant. You've escaped the outbreak's epicenter. But the world beyond is uncertain.

choices.description: The tunnels twist and turn. You get lost. Eventually, you hear voices and follow them back to Rosa's group.
