choices.label: Turn back to Rosa's group

script.content: You back away from the tunnel survivors, raising your hands. 'No problem. I'll find my own way.'
You disappear into the darkness of the tunnel. The whispers of the group fade behind you. You're alone in the underground, with only the sound of dripping water and your own footsteps.

The tunnels branch and twist. You navigate by feel, keeping your hand on the damp wall. After what feels like hours, you see a faint light ahead—a manhole cover with daylight streaming through the cracks.

choices.description: Delroy leads you to a maintenance van in the garage. The keys are inside. You drive toward the exit ramp, but a collapsed concrete barrier blocks the way. You'll need to clear it or find another path.
choices.label: Clear the rubble with Delroy and Marcus
choices.targetSceneDescription: Together, you move enough rubble to squeeze the van through. You emerge onto a side street. Delroy knows a route to the stadium that avoids main roads. You drive through back alleys, making slow but steady progress.

choices.description: The garage is a dead end. You, Marcus, and Delroy go back up to street level through the stairwell.
choices.label: Abandon the garage and go back up

script.content: Delroy leads you through the dark parking garage, his flashlight cutting through the blackness. Rows of cars sit silently, their windows glinting in the beam.
You find a maintenance van with keys in the cup holder. Jackpot. The engine turns over smoothly.
But as you approach the exit ramp, your headlights illuminate a problem—a collapsed concrete barrier blocks the way. Rubble and rebar form a wall across the ramp.
We could move it. Maybe. If we work together.

choices.description: The lobby survivors are preparing to move. They've heard about the stadium evacuation too. You join their group as they exit the building into the street.
choices.label: Join the lobby survivors

choices.description: You and Marcus slip out the side door. The alley leads to a side street. You need to decide where to go from here.
choices.label: Exit through the side door

script.content: You descend the stairs and push open the lobby door. A dozen faces turn toward you. Hands reach for weapons, then stop as they see you're human.
Jesus! Don't sneak up on people like that!
The group is a mix of office workers, security personnel, and a janitor. They've barricaded the main entrance but know they can't hold forever.
We've been debating what to do. Some want to make a run for the stadium. Others want to wait for rescue. What do you think?

choices.description: The police station is fortified. Officers check you for bites and wave you inside. There are dozens of survivors here. It's a safe zone, if not a comfortable one.
choices.label: Stay at the police station
choices.targetSceneDescription: You and Marcus settle into the police station. It's crowded but organized. Officers have set up a command post and are coordinating with the military. A evacuation convoy is being organized to take everyone to the stadium.

choices.description: You learn that the police are organizing a convoy to the stadium. You decide to join it rather than stay put.
choices.label: Join the evacuation convoy

script.content: You find an alternate route around the collapse and the police station appears ahead. It's a fortress—sandbags, patrol cars forming a perimeter, armed officers watching every approach.
You pull up to the checkpoint. An officer approaches, weapon ready. 'Cut the engine. Step out slow.'
You comply. They check you and Marcus for bites. Clean. You're waved through the perimeter.
Welcome to the last safe block in the city. For now.

choices.description: You move deeper into the parking garage. The upper levels are dark, but you can see light filtering through ventilation grates. You hear the scraping sound again—closer now.
choices.label: Investigate the scraping sound
choices.targetSceneDescription: You ascend to the upper level of the parking garage. The source of the scraping becomes clear—a survivor is trying to push a car off a ledge to create a distraction below. She's a young woman, alone and terrified. She nearly attacks you before realizing you're human.

choices.description: You decide the garage is a trap. You turn the bike around and head back out, looking for another path.
choices.label: Leave the garage

script.content: You duck into the parking garage, the engine echoing off concrete walls. The sudden dimness makes you blink. Row after row of parked cars stretches into the darkness.
From the upper levels, you hear a scraping sound—something heavy being dragged across concrete.
We're not alone in here.

choices.description: You settle into the stadium camp. It's crowded, chaotic, but safe. You find a spot against a wall and close your eyes. The nightmare is over—for now.
choices.label: Rest and recover
choices.targetSceneDescription: You've reached safety. The stadium is a sanctuary, packed with thousands of other survivors. The military maintains order. You've lost everything, but you've gained something precious: another day. The story continues, but this chapter is over. You survived.

choices.description: Rumors swirl in the camp—some say the infection is spreading beyond the city, others say the military is planning to bomb the city to contain it. You decide to find out the truth.
choices.label: Investigate the rumors
choices.targetSceneDescription: You talk to soldiers, aid workers, and other survivors. The truth is worse than you feared: the infection is airborne in some areas, and the military is considering a quarantine firebombing of the city. The stadium might not be safe for long.

script.content: The stadium looms before you, massive and imposing. Thousands of survivors are gathered in and around it. Military vehicles form a perimeter. Tents stretch across the parking lot.
You pass through the checkpoint. A soldier hands you a bottle of water and a blanket. 'Welcome to the evacuation zone. You're safe now.'
Inside the stadium, people sit in clusters on the field and in the stands. Families, couples, lone survivors. The mood is somber but hopeful. You've made it.
You find a spot to sit. For the first time since the outbreak began, you allow yourself to breathe.

choices.description: You reach down and grab Marcus's hand. He clings to you, his weight nearly pulling you off the ladder. But you hold on. Together, you climb to safety.
choices.label: Pull Marcus up

choices.description: You can't hold on. Marcus slips. You watch him fall, disappearing into the horde below. You close your eyes and climb.
choices.label: Watch Marcus fall

script.content: You cling to the rope ladder, the helicopter ascending. Below, Marcus fights alone, surrounded. He looks up and sees you on the ladder.
GO! Just GO!
But then he makes a break for it—sprinting toward the ladder, cutting through the infected with his crowbar. He leaps, his hand grabbing the bottom rung just as the helicopter climbs higher.
He's dangling below you, his weight threatening to pull the ladder loose. You have to decide now.

choices.description: You sit in the helicopter, alone with your thoughts. The medic bandages your wounds. The city disappears into the smoke. You survived. That will have to be enough.
choices.label: Accept the solitude

choices.description: You demand the pilot take you back. 'There are more survivors!' you shout. 'We can't just leave them!'
choices.label: Demand to go back

script.content: You're pulled into the helicopter. The soldier slams the door shut. Below, through the window, you see the rooftop disappear—and with it, Marcus.
The helicopter banks away from the city. The burning skyline fills the window. A medic checks your wounds, saying something you can't hear over the rotor noise.
You're alive. That's what matters. That's what everyone will tell you. But as you fly away from the ruins of your city, you can't help but feel like you left a part of yourself behind.

choices.description: You and Marcus slump against the helicopter wall, gasping. A medic hands you both water. Marcus meets your eyes and nods once. No words needed.
choices.label: Share the moment with Marcus
choices.targetSceneDescription: You and Marcus made it out together. Two strangers who became allies, who became friends. The road ahead is uncertain, but you won't walk it alone.

choices.description: You look out the window as the city burns below. You think about everyone you've lost. But you're here, you're alive, and you'll carry their memories forward.
choices.label: Look out at the burning city

script.content: You grab Marcus's hand and haul him aboard. He tumbles into the helicopter, gasping. An infected lunges after him, but a soldier kicks it back into the void and slams the door.
The helicopter banks hard. You and Marcus slide across the metal floor, landing in a heap. For a long moment, neither of you speaks—just breathing, just being alive.
You... you came back for me.
We're in this together. That's what you said, right?
The helicopter carries you both away from the burning city. Below, the world you knew crumbles into ash. But above the clouds, a new world is waiting.

choices.description: You join the march through the city. The group moves quickly, staying to shadows. You encounter infected three times, fighting through each time. The stadium gates appear just as dusk falls.
choices.label: March with the group

choices.description: The group is too large and too loud. You break off from them, choosing to make your own way to the stadium.
choices.label: Go solo to the stadium

script.content: The group assembles in the lobby. Twelve people, ranging from office workers to security guards. Makeshift weapons in hand. Fear in every eye.
Alright, listen up! We're heading to the stadium. It's three miles east. Stay together, stay quiet, and we'll make it.
You file out the back entrance. The streets are quiet—too quiet. The infected are out there, but for now, they're hidden. You move in a tight formation, checking every intersection.
The journey takes hours. Twice you hide from passing hordes. Once, you fight—losing one of your group. But the stadium grows closer with every step.

choices.description: The barricade holds for days. But eventually, the infected come in force. You fight alongside Rivera and the others. It's a good last stand.
choices.label: Make your last stand
choices.targetSceneDescription: The barricade falls. You fight until the end, surrounded by the people who became your family in the darkest of times. The world may have ended, but you faced it on your feet.

choices.description: When the barricade comes under attack, you slip away in the chaos, heading for the stadium alone.
choices.label: Escape in the chaos

script.content: Days pass at the barricade. You fall into a rhythm—watch, sleep, scavenge, watch again. The infected grow bolder. Supplies dwindle.
On the third night, they come in force. A wave of infected, dozens strong, crashes against the barricade. Sandbags shift. Cars rock. The defenders fight with everything they have.
Rivera falls beside you, his gun empty. You grab his weapon and keep firing. But there are too many. The barricade is breached.

choices.description: You follow Rosa's group through the storm drain. The tunnel is dark and claustrophobic, but it leads beyond the quarantine zone. You emerge into a forest on the outskirts of the city.
choices.label: Escape through the storm drain
choices.targetSceneDescription: You emerge from the tunnel into a dense forest. The sounds of the city are distant. You're free. Rosa's group has a camp nearby. You've found a new family and a new home.

choices.description: Halfway through the tunnel, you hear voices ahead—not Rosa's group. Raiders. You turn back, leaving the group to their fate.
choices.label: Turn back and go your own way

script.content: Rosa leads the group through the winding tunnels. Children cling to their parents. The adults carry what supplies they have. The only light comes from flashlights and a few dim emergency bulbs.
The storm drain is just ahead. It leads under the quarantine wall. Once we're out, we're in the uninfected zone.
The tunnel narrows. Water trickles around your ankles. The sound of dripping echoes all around you. Then you see it—a grate, with moonlight streaming through.
Rosa works the bolts free. The grate swings open. Fresh air floods in. Freedom.

choices.description: Together, you and Delroy clear enough rubble to squeeze the van through. You emerge onto a side street. Delroy knows a route to the stadium that avoids main roads.
choices.label: Clear the rubble together

choices.description: The rubble is too heavy. You search the garage and find a service elevator. It's risky, but it might take you to the roof where you can cross to another building.
choices.label: Take the service elevator up

script.content: You, Marcus, and Delroy work together to move the rubble. It's exhausting, dangerous work. The concrete is heavy, and you're all on edge, listening for infected.
Almost there! Just a few more pieces!
You shift the last piece of rubble. The path is clear. You pile into the van, and Delroy takes the wheel. The engine echoes through the garage as you speed toward the exit ramp.
You burst out onto the street. Sunlight floods the cabin. You're moving. You're alive.

choices.description: You settle into the police station. It's organized and safe. Officers coordinate with the military. You're assigned a cot and a meal. You've found refuge.
choices.label: Stay at the station

choices.description: The police are organizing a convoy to the stadium. You decide to join it, hoping the larger safe zone offers more long-term security.
choices.label: Join the convoy

script.content: The police station is a hive of activity. Officers coordinate on radios, medics tend to the wounded, and volunteers distribute food and water.
Welcome to the last safe block. Name's Officer Daniels. Let's get you checked out.
You're given a cot in a conference room. Other survivors sit quietly, staring at nothing. The weight of everything you've been through settles on your shoulders.
An officer announces that a convoy will be heading to the stadium evacuation point tomorrow. You have a choice to make.

choices.description: You carefully ascend to the upper level. The source of the scraping becomes clear—a young woman is trying to push a car off the edge to create a distraction below. She's terrified but tough.
choices.label: Approach the woman cautiously
choices.targetSceneDescription: The woman, whose name is Jade, was hiding in the garage when the outbreak hit. She's been surviving alone for days. She knows a route to the stadium through the maintenance tunnels. She offers to guide you.

choices.description: The scraping sound could be a trap. You decide to leave the garage quietly and continue on foot.
choices.label: Leave the garage quietly

script.content: You ascend the concrete ramp to the upper level of the parking garage. The scraping sound grows louder. You peer between rows of parked cars.
You see her—a young woman with a streak of gray in her dark hair, her hands bloody from shoving against the bumper of an old sedan. She's trying to push it off the ledge.
She senses you before she sees you. She spins, a tire iron in her hand, ready to fight.
Whoa! I'm not infected! I'm just trying to get out of this city!

choices.description: You climb through the broken window into a dark, ransacked apartment. A radio on the kitchen counter crackles with static—then clears. '...stadium... evacuation... repeat... military evacuation at the football stadium...'
choices.label: Listen to the radio

choices.description: You search the apartment for supplies. You find a backpack, some canned food, and a map of the city. The stadium is marked three miles east.
choices.label: Search for supplies

script.content: You squeeze through the broken window, landing silently on a carpeted floor. You're in an apartment—someone's home, now abandoned. Furniture is overturned, drawers pulled out.
A radio on the kitchen counter flickers with a blinking red light. It's picking up a signal. You turn up the volume.

A distorted recording loops: '...this is an emergency broadcast... military evacuation in progress at the football stadium... all survivors are advised to make their way to the stadium... repeat... the stadium is a designated safe zone...'

choices.description: Armed with the handgun, you feel more confident. You and Mrs. Gutierrez head for the stairwell. The journey ahead is dangerous, but you're ready.
choices.label: Head for the stadium

choices.description: You strap the gun to your hip and lead Mrs. Gutierrez through the building's back exit, hoping to avoid the main streets.
choices.label: Take the back exit

script.content: You check the handgun. It's loaded. The weight of it in your hand changes something—you're not just prey anymore. You're a survivor.
I don't like guns. But I like those things out there even less.
You pack the supplies into your backpack: canned food, water, first-aid kit, ammunition. Mrs. Gutierrez finds a sturdy walking stick and hefts it like a club.
Together, you leave the apartment for the last time. The hallway is empty. The stairwell is quiet. Somewhere out there, the stadium waits.

choices.description: You head toward the stadium, visible above the rooftops. The journey is long but clear. You arrive at the gates as dusk falls.
choices.label: Head to the stadium

choices.description: You decide to explore the neighborhood first, hoping to find more supplies or other survivors.
choices.label: Explore the neighborhood

script.content: The radio message repeats on a loop. The stadium. That's where you need to go. You memorize the directions and turn off the radio to save the batteries.
The stadium... I used to go there with my husband. Football games. Concerts. It seems like another life now.
You leave the apartment and emerge onto the street. The stadium rises in the distance, a beacon of hope against the smoke-filled sky. You start walking.

choices.description: You follow the highway out of the city. The road stretches ahead, empty and open. You've left the nightmare behind. Ahead lies only the unknown.
choices.label: Drive into the unknown

choices.description: You don't leave. You find a high point on the highway and look back at the city one last time. So much loss. But you're still here.
choices.label: Look back at the city

script.content: You clear the last row of abandoned cars. The highway opens up before you—clear asphalt stretching toward the horizon. The city is behind you.
You stop for a moment and look back. The city skyline is shrouded in smoke. Fires flicker like candles on a birthday cake for the dead. You turn away.
The road ahead is empty. Quiet. The world beyond the city is unknown—it could be safe, or it could be worse. But for the first time since the outbreak began, you have a choice. You're free.

choices.description: You climb aboard the troop transport. The soldiers are heading to reinforce the stadium. You're going back into danger, but with support. This time, you're not alone.
choices.label: Ride with the convoy

choices.description: The convoy is too large, too slow. You wave them on and continue on foot, moving faster on your own.
choices.label: Continue on foot

script.content: The convoy rumbles to a halt. Armored vehicles, troop transports, supply trucks. A soldier jumps down from the lead vehicle, weapon ready.
You a survivor? Get in the transport. We're heading to the stadium to reinforce the evacuation.
You climb aboard. The transport is full of young soldiers, their faces pale with fear but their eyes hard with determination. One of them hands you a rifle.
You know how to use one of these?
You made it. Against all odds, against the darkness that swallowed the world, you survived.
The road ahead is uncertain. The infection is still out there. Friends are lost. The world will never be the same. But you're still breathing. You're still fighting. You're still you.
This is not the end of your story. This is just the beginning.

choices.description: The rumors are true. The military is considering firebombing the city. You need to get out—now. You make plans to leave the camp.
choices.label: Plan to escape the camp

choices.description: You decide to confront the military command about the rumors. If they're planning to destroy the city, there must be another way.
choices.label: Confront the commanders

script.content: You move through the camp, listening. Whispers travel faster than news here. The stories are all different, but they share a dark thread.
I heard they're going to firebomb the whole city. Containment protocol. They're not evacuating us—they're just getting us out of the blast zone.
Your blood runs cold. You look up at the stadium walls, suddenly feeling less like a sanctuary and more like a cage.
You need to find out the truth. And you need to decide what to do with it.
You and Marcus stand side by side, looking out at the uncertain future. Two strangers who became brothers in the fire.
What now?
We survive. Together.
And that's exactly what you do.
The barricade falls. The infected pour through. You fight with everything you have, side by side with the people who became your family.
You take down three, four, five of them. But there are always more. Your weapon breaks. Your body gives out.
As the world fades, you think of the choices you made, the people you met, the battles you fought. You did not go quietly into that good night. You raged against the dying of the light.
And in the end, that's all anyone can do.
You step out of the darkness and into the light. The sun is warm on your face. The air smells of trees, not smoke. The sounds of the city are gone.
You're free. The infection, the chaos, the death—it's all behind you. Ahead lies a world waiting to be rebuilt.
The nightmare is over. But the dream is just beginning.

choices.description: You find Jade and follow her through the maintenance tunnels. She knows the city's underground like the back of her hand. After an hour of navigating, you emerge near the stadium.
choices.label: Follow Jade through the tunnels

choices.description: You thank Jade but decide to go alone. The tunnels could be a trap.
choices.label: Go alone

script.content: The woman lowers her tire iron slightly. 'You're not one of them?' Her voice is hoarse, like she hasn't spoken in days.
No. I'm trying to get to the stadium. Military evacuation.
The stadium? That's where I was heading. I'm Jade. I've been hiding in this garage for three days. I know a way through the maintenance tunnels that'll get us there without going through the streets.

Apartment 3C.name: Apartment 3C
Apartment 3C.vignette: Your small, cluttered one-bedroom apartment. The power is out, leaving everything bathed in an oppressive darkness punctuated only by the faint orange glow of distant fires through the window.
Apartment 3C.appearanceDescription: A modest apartment with a living room, kitchenette, bedroom, and a fire escape balcony. The furniture is disheveled from panic. A front door leads to the hallway, and a window overlooks the alley below.
Apartment 3C.backstoryDescription: You've lived here for three years. It's your sanctuary, but now its thin walls and single exit make it feel like a trap.

The Hallway.name: The Hallway
The Hallway.vignette: The narrow, dimly lit corridor of your apartment building's third floor. Emergency lights flicker weakly, casting long, dancing shadows. The air smells of smoke and something metallic.
The Hallway.appearanceDescription: Carpeted hallway with numbered doors on either side. A stairwell door at one end, a window at the other overlooking the street. Flickering emergency lights create an eerie atmosphere.
The Hallway.backstoryDescription: Once a mundane passage you walked daily, now a potential death trap with unknown horrors lurking around corners.

The Alleyway.name: The Alleyway
The Alleyway.vignette: A narrow, garbage-strewn alley running between your building and the next. Dumpsters overflow with trash, and the broken glass from a shattered window glitters menacingly in the firelight.
The Alleyway.appearanceDescription: Dark, cramped, and reeking of rot. A chain-link fence blocks one end. Puddles of unknown liquid reflect the orange glow of the burning city.
The Alleyway.backstoryDescription: Normally an unremarkable urban space, now echoing with guttural howls and the sounds of chaos.

The Rooftop.name: The Rooftop
The Rooftop.vignette: The flat, tar-paper roof of the apartment building. HVAC units and abandoned patio furniture dot the space. From here, you can see the city burning in the distance, a hellish panorama of smoke and flame.
The Rooftop.appearanceDescription: Open sky above, a ladder access from below, and a low wall around the perimeter. The wind whips fiercely, carrying ash and the distant sounds of screams and sirens.
The Rooftop.backstoryDescription: A forgotten space where tenants occasionally sunbathed. Now it might be your only escape route or your final stand.

Street Level.name: Street Level
Street Level.vignette: The chaotic urban battlefield that your quiet street has become. Overturned cars burn like bonfires. Shadows move erratically between the flames. The city's familiar skyline is obscured by thick, black smoke.
Street Level.appearanceDescription: Broken asphalt littered with debris, abandoned vehicles, and things best not examined too closely. The street signs hang crooked, and storefronts are smashed open.
Street Level.backstoryDescription: What was once a normal city street is now a war zone. The outbreak has transformed the familiar into something terrifying.

You.name: You
You.vignette: A survivor. You were just an ordinary person living an ordinary life when the world ended. Now you must make choices that will determine if you live to see tomorrow.
You.appearanceDescription: You look like yourself - disheveled, wide-eyed, gripping whatever you could grab in the chaos.
You.backstoryDescription: Your past doesn't matter now. Only what you do next.

Mrs. Gutierrez.name: Mrs. Gutierrez
Mrs. Gutierrez.vignette: Your elderly neighbor from apartment 3D. She's a kind widow who always brought you homemade cookies during the holidays. Now her voice is choked with terror as she pounds on your door.
Mrs. Gutierrez.appearanceDescription: A small woman in her late 60s, gray hair disheveled, wearing a floral nightgown and slippers. Her eyes are wide with primal fear.
Mrs. Gutierrez.backstoryDescription: She's lived in this building for thirty years. Her husband passed away two years ago. She has no family nearby.

The Infected.name: The Infected
The Infected.vignette: Former humans, now twisted by whatever catastrophe has befallen the city. They move with an unnatural, jerky speed, driven by a ravenous hunger that has erased all traces of their humanity.
The Infected.appearanceDescription: Pale, blood-streaked skin. Eyes that are fully black or filmed over white. Clothes torn and stained. They move with a shuddering, predatory gait.
The Infected.backstoryDescription: No one knows exactly what caused the转变. Something in the air, the water, or perhaps something that was always sleeping inside humanity has now awakened.

Marcus.name: Marcus
Marcus.vignette: A man you recognize from the building - he lives on the second floor. You've seen him fixing his motorcycle in the parking lot. He's tough, practical, and has the look of someone who's been through hard times before.
Marcus.appearanceDescription: Late 30s, muscular build, tattooed arms, short-cropped hair. He wears a leather jacket over a grey shirt, jeans, and heavy boots. He carries a crowbar.
Marcus.backstoryDescription: An army veteran who keeps to himself. He's been preparing for something like this for years, though he never said so out loud.
